transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Thanks... honestly, ever since the shooting I feel like I’m constantly on guard, checking every room and jumpy about anything happening around me. I just can't seem to shake this feeling.
Since the shooting, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks that make you feel like it’s happening again?
No, I haven't really been having nightmares or flashbacks of the shooting. To be honest, I actually have a hard time remembering the actual event itself, like there's a chunk of it that's just blank.
Since the shooting, have you been avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of it, or feeling emotionally numb or detached from others?

Yes, I've been avoiding nightlife spots and even skipped a major evening client event at a bar because I just couldn't face going back there. I also feel completely numb and disconnected from everyone; when my team closed a big deal, I felt totally flat and unable to feel happy. It honestly feels like I'm just watching my life like a movie, floating outside my own body.
Have these symptoms lasted for more than one month since the shooting?
No, it hasn't been a month. The shooting only happened about ten days ago, so these problems have just been going on for about a week and a half.
Have you had any moments where you felt completely dazed, confused, or unable to respond to what was happening around you since the shooting?

Yes, absolutely. My brain feels so fogged out that I'll lose my train of thought mid-sentence and just stare blankly at my computer screen, unable to make simple decisions. It often feels like I'm dazed and moving through a movie of my own life, with everything around me looking washed out and sounding far away.
Have you had any episodes where you completely lost time, could not remember what you did, or found yourself somewhere without knowing how you got there?

No, I don't wander off to random places or lose track of where I am. But I do have a complete black hole in my memory for the exact moment the shooting started, even though I remember everything right before and after. And while I sometimes feel like I'm floating outside my body watching myself, I still know exactly where I physically am.
During these episodes, do you ever lose track of who you are or where you are, or find yourself doing things and later not remembering them at all?

No, I don't lose track of who I am or find myself doing things I can't remember. I just have that specific black hole in my memory for the exact moments of the shooting, even though I remember everything before and after clearly. When I feel detached, it's more like I'm watching my life play out in a movie, rather than actually losing my identity.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than one month since the shooting, or have they continued for more than a month?
Yes, it has definitely been less than a month. It's only been about ten days since the night of the shooting, and all of these issues started right after it happened.
Since the shooting, have you had moments where things around you felt unreal or dreamlike, or where you felt detached from your body or like you were watching yourself from outside?

Yes, exactly. A lot of the time, it feels like I'm moving through a movie of my life where voices sound far away and colors look washed out. It really does feel like I'm floating just outside my own body, watching myself go through the motions.

Have you ever had a period of time after the shooting where you completely lost awareness of where you were or what you were doing, or found that you had no memory for actions you took during that time?

No, I haven't lost awareness or forgotten any of my actions after the shooting; I actually remember everything after that night all too clearly. The only memory gap I have is the specific moment when the guy pulled the gun and started firing, which is just a complete black hole.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed symptoms within 10 days of a clearly identified traumatic event (a shooting), including marked anxiety/hypervigilance, startle/jumpiness, emotional numbing, avoidance of reminders, dissociative symptoms (derealization/depersonalization), and a partial amnesia for the traumatic moment. The duration is under 1 month, making acute stress reaction the best fit.
